Rashi on Niddah 41a:10:1.english: For a non-sacred animal - And he consecrated it.

Rashi on Niddah 41a:11:1.hebrew: המקשה ג' ימים - בימי זיבה, וראתה דם כל שלשה דרך רחם:
Rashi on Niddah 41a:11:1.english: A woman who experiences difficult labor for three days - [This occurred] during the days of ziva, and she saw blood all three [days] by way of the womb.

Rashi on Niddah 41a:11:2.hebrew: ויצא ולד דרך דופן הרי זו יולדת בזוב - כלומר, זבה היא, דכי טיהר רחמנא מזיבה דם הקושי, הני מילי בלידה מעלייתא, אבל דרך דופן לאו לידה היא:
Rashi on Niddah 41a:11:2.english: And the offspring emerged via caesarean section, she is one who gives birth during ziva - That is to say, she is a zava; for when the Merciful One deemed the blood of travail pure from [the impurity of] ziva, this applies only to a proper birth, but [emergence] via caesarean section is not [considered] a birth.

Rashi on Niddah 41a:11:3.hebrew: אין זו יולדת בזוב - ור"ש לטעמיה, דאמר: יוצא דופן ולד מעליא הוא, ומטהר את קישויו:
Rashi on Niddah 41a:11:3.english: She is not one who gives birth during zivah - And Rabbi Shimon [is consistent] with his reasoning, as he says that [an offspring born by] caesarean section is a valid offspring, and it purifies [the blood of] its labor.

Rashi on Niddah 41a:11:4.english: And the blood that emerges from there - Later [the Gemara] explains what it is saying.

Rashi on Niddah 41a:12:1.hebrew: ר"ש לטעמיה - דאמר במתניתין: יושבין עליו ימי טומאה, אפילו בלידה יבשתא, וימי טהרה, אלמא ולד הוא. הלכך, לענין קושי נמי ולד הוא, ומטהר את קישויו:
Rashi on Niddah 41a:12:1.english: Rabbi Shimon [follows] his reasoning - For he stated in the mishna [that] one observes on its account the days of impurity, even in a dry birth, and the days of purity, which shows that it is an offspring. Therefore, with regard to [labor] pangs as well, it is an offspring, and it purifies [the blood of] her labor pangs.

Rashi on Niddah 41a:12:2.hebrew: אלא סיפא במאי פליגי - הא ליכא למימר: דם היוצא עמו דרך דופן יהיה טמא כדם הלידה, דאם כן, איפכא מבעי ליה: רבי שמעון מטמא, דאמר ולד הוא, וחכמים מטהרים. אלא ודאי, אפי' לרבי שמעון לא הוי אלא כדם המכה. והא דאמר רבי שמעון במתניתין יושבין עליו ימי טומאה - משום ולד קאמר, ולא משום דם:
Rashi on Niddah 41a:12:2.english: Rather, in the latter clause, about what do they disagree - For one cannot say that the blood that emerges with it through the abdominal wall should be impure like the blood of childbirth, for if so, it should have been the reverse: Rabbi Shimon should deem it impure, as he says that it is an offspring, and the Sages should deem it pure. Rather, it is certain that even according to Rabbi Shimon, it is nothing other than the blood of a wound. And that which Rabbi Shimon said in the mishna, "They observe for it the days of impurity," he said this on account of the offspring, and not on account of the blood.

Rashi on Niddah 41a:1:1.hebrew: אחר שריבה הכתוב ומיעט אמרת כו' - הואיל וכתוב אחד ריבה וכתוב אחד מיעט, מעתה יש לך לילך אחר אומד הדעת:
Rashi on Niddah 41a:1:1.english: After the verse included and excluded, you say, etc. - Since one verse included and one verse excluded, you must now follow reasoned assessment.

Rashi on Niddah 41a:1:2.english: I include those whose disqualification was in the sacred [area] - That their disqualification occurred after they came to the [Temple] courtyard.

Rashi on Niddah 41a:3:1.hebrew: מפטר רחם נפקא - דלא קדיש, וכיון דחולין הוא, למה לי למעוטי? פשיטא, אם עלה ירד:
Rashi on Niddah 41a:3:1.english: Is derived from "that which opens the womb" - That it is not sacred; and since it is unconsecrated, why do I need to exclude it? It is obvious: if it went up [onto the altar], it must descend.

Rashi on Niddah 41a:4:1.hebrew: מאמו אמו נפקא - נמי דלא קדיש, דגמר מבכור:
Rashi on Niddah 41a:4:1.english: It is derived from "its mother" [and] "its mother" - It is also [derived] that it is not consecrated, as it derives from a firstborn.

Rashi on Niddah 41a:5:1.english: Two verses - [The verbal analogy of] "its mother," "its mother," and [the verse] "this."

Rashi on Niddah 41a:5:2.hebrew: חד לבהמה דחולין ואוליד דרך דופן ואקדשיה - ושמעינן מאמו אמו דלא קדיש. וחד לבהמה דקדשים, דעל כרחך ולד היוצא ממנה קדוש מאליו, ואיצטריך למעוטי מזאת, דאע"ג דקדיש, אם עלה ירד, הואיל ולא היה פסולו בקדש:
Rashi on Niddah 41a:5:2.english: One for a non-sacred animal that gave birth via caesarean section and [its owner] consecrated it - And we learn from [the verbal analogy of] "its mother" [and] "its mother" that it does not become sacred. And one [verse is needed] for a consecrated animal, where perforce the offspring that emerges from it is sacred on its own, and it was necessary to exclude it from "This" [is the law of the burnt offering, teaching] that even though it is sacred, if it ascended [the altar], it must descend, since its disqualification was not in the sacred.

Rashi on Niddah 41a:6:1.hebrew: וקסבר ולדות קדשים בהוייתן הן קדושין - נראה בעיני דלא גרסי' ליה, ופירוש משובש הוא, דכל שכן למאן דאמר משעת יצירה הן קדושים, דהיינו במעי אמו, דאיצטריך למעוטי מזאת:
Rashi on Niddah 41a:6:1.english: And he maintains that the offspring of sacrificial animals are sacred upon their emergence - It appears to me that we should not read this [in the text], and it is an erroneous explanation; for all the more so according to the one who says that they are sacred from the time of formation, that is, in its mother's womb, was it necessary to exclude [it] from "this" [verse].

Rashi on Niddah 41a:7:1.hebrew: הכי נמי מסתברא - דכל הני פסולין דהכא, בבהמות קדשים קאמר. ורובע ונרבע, כגון שהקדישן ולבסוף נרבעו. ומוקצה ונעבד נמי, בקדשים קלים, ואליבא דרבי יוסי הגלילי, דאמר: ממון בעלים הן, ויכול לאוסרן; והכי נמי מוקמינן בפרק בתרא דזבחים (דף קיד.). ואתנן ומחיר, כשנתן לה עובר בהמת קדשים קלים באתנן, וקסבר: בהוייתן הם קדושים ולא קודם לכן, לפיכך איסור אתנן ומחיר חל עליהם, וקדושה דממילא נמי חיילא עלייהו, והרי הם קדושים. וכלאים וטרפה ויוצא דופן נמי, בולדות קדשים:
Rashi on Niddah 41a:7:1.english: So too, it is reasonable - That with regard to all of these disqualified [animals mentioned] here, [the baraita] is speaking of consecrated animals. And an animal that copulated [with a person] and an animal that was the object of bestiality: for example, where one consecrated them and afterwards they were subjected to bestiality. And an animal set aside [for idol worship] and an animal that was worshipped [as a deity] as well: in [the case of] offerings of lesser sanctity, and in accordance with [the view of] Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who says: They are the monetary property of the owner, and [therefore] he can render them forbidden; and so too we establish [the baraita] in the final chapter of Zevachim (page 114a). And the payment [of a prostitute] and the price [of a dog]: where one gave her the fetus of an animal of lesser sanctity as payment [to a prostitute], and [the Tanna] maintains that they become sacred upon their emergence [into the world], and not prior to that; therefore, the prohibition of the payment [of a prostitute] and the price [of a dog] takes effect upon them, and automatic sanctity also takes effect upon them, and behold, they are sacred. And [an animal of] diverse kinds, and a tereifah, and an animal born by caesarean section as well: in [the case of] the offspring of consecrated animals.

Rashi on Niddah 41a:7:2.hebrew: הכי נמי מסתברא - דבקדשים קאי, ותרי קראי איצטריכא ליה כדאמר, מדקתני הרובע והנרבע, וקא ממעט להו מהאי קרא. וכי מהכא נפקא? מהתם נפקא:
Rashi on Niddah 41a:7:2.english: So too, it is reasonable - That [the baraita] is dealing with sacrificial animals, and two verses were needed for it, as [the Gemara] said, from the fact that it teaches: "An animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was the object of bestiality," and excludes them from this verse. And do they derive from here? They derive from there!

Rashi on Niddah 41a:8:1.hebrew: מן הבהמה - אדם כי יקריב מכם מן הבהמה, ולא כל בהמה, להוציא את הרובע והנרבע:
Rashi on Niddah 41a:8:1.english: From the animal - [The verse states:] "[When] a person from among you brings [an offering] from the animal" — and not every animal, to exclude an animal that copulated [with a person] and [an animal] that was copulated with.

Rashi on Niddah 41a:8:2.hebrew: נוגח - שהמית את האדם. והאי רובע ונרבע ונוגח דקתני - כגון על פי עד אחד, או על פי הבעלים, דמודה בקנס פטור; הלכך, להדיוט שרי, ולגבוה אסור. אבל ע"פ שני עדים - בסקילה הוא, ולהדיוט נמי אסור:
Rashi on Niddah 41a:8:2.english: [An animal] that gored - That killed a person. And this [case of] an animal that copulated [with a person], or was the object of bestiality, or that gored, which is taught [here, is referring to a case] such as based on [the testimony of] a single witness, or based on [the confession of] the owner, for one who admits to a fine is exempt. Therefore, it is permitted to an ordinary person, but forbidden to the Most High. But based on [the testimony of] two witnesses, it is [subject] to stoning, and is forbidden to an ordinary person as well.

Rashi on Niddah 41a:9:1.english: Diverse kinds - [An animal born] from a goat and from a sheep.

Rashi on Niddah 41a:9:2.hebrew: נדמה - אביו ואמו מן העז, והוא כבש. וכיון דנפקי מהתם דלא קדש, למה לי למעוטי מהכא דירדו? הא חולין נינהו:
Rashi on Niddah 41a:9:2.english: An animal that resembles [another] - Its father and its mother are of the goat [species], but it [resembles] a sheep. And since they are derived from there [to teach] that they do not become consecrated, why do I need to exclude [them] from here [to teach] that they must descend? Surely they are non-sacred [animals]!

Tosafot on Niddah 41a:12:1.hebrew: ורבנן לטעמייהו - וא"ת: אע"ג דלא מטמאי לידה, מ"מ ליטהר דם קישויה, דאפי' בהפילה רוח פריך בפ"ק (לעיל נדה דף ח:) שיהא קישויה טהור, אע"ג דאין נותנין לה ימי טומאה וימי טהרה. ויש לומר: דהתם משום דבעי למימר דמיקרי לידה, כדמייתי קרא כמו ילדנו רוח; אבל הכא, מיעטיה קרא מדין ולד:
Tosafot on Niddah 41a:12:1.english: And the Rabbis [conform] to their line of reasoning - And if you say: Even though they do not deem [her] impure [with the impurity of] childbirth, nevertheless let the blood of her labor pains be pure! For even regarding [a woman who] miscarried wind, [the Gemara] asks in the first chapter (above, Niddah 8b) that [the blood of] her labor pains should be pure, even though one does not assign to her days of impurity and days of purity. And one can say: There, [it is] because [the Gemara] wanted to say that it is called childbirth, as it cites the verse: "we have as it were brought forth wind" (Isaiah 26:18); but here, Scripture excluded it from the legal status of an offspring.

Tosafot on Niddah 41a:1:1.hebrew: שהיה פסולן בקדש - שאין פסולן יכול להיות עד אחר שהוקדש, אבל רובע ונרבע מצי להיות בעודן חולין. וקשה, דאמרינן בזבחים פ' חטאת העוף (זבחים דף סח:): זר וסכין מטמאין, אלמא חשיב אין פסולן בקדש, אע"ג דלא שייכי עד לאחר שהוקדש; ושמאל ולילה נמי הוה מטמאין, אי לאו דאית להו הכשר במקום אחר, כדאמר התם; ודוקין שבעין, קאמר רבי עקיבא דאם עלו לא ירדו משום דכשר בעוף, אלמא חשיב פסולו בקודש, אע"ג דיכול להיות קודם הקדש! ונראה לפרש, דהיכא דכיוצא בו כשר במקום אחר, קרי פסולו בקדש: ונשחט בלילה אית ליה הכשר באברים ופדרים; ויוצא דמה שכן כשר באימורים, ואימורים שכן כשר בבמה; ונשפך דמה, כיון שקבלה היתה בהכשר, מיקרי פסולו בקדש. ולשון פסולו בקדש היינו שאין כאן פסול גמור, אלא נפסל בקדושתו. וכן משמע דפריך התם: מ"ש שמאל דאית ליה הכשר ביום הכיפורים ולילה באברים ופדרין, ולכך אין מטמאין, דהוי פסולן בקדש:
Tosafot on Niddah 41a:1:1.english: Whose disqualification was in the sacred - That their disqualification cannot possibly occur until after [the animal] has been consecrated; whereas [the disqualification of an animal that] copulated with a person or was the object of bestiality can occur while they are still unconsecrated. And this is difficult, for we say in Zevachim, in the chapter [entitled] "Ḥatat HaOf" (Zevachim 68b): [Pinching by] a non-priest (zar) and [pinching with] a knife defile [in the throat]. This proves that [the Gemara] considers [these as cases where] their disqualification was not in the sacred, even though they are inapplicable until after [the bird] has been consecrated! And [pinching with] the left [hand] and at night would also defile, were it not that they have [an instance of] fitness in another context, as [the Gemara] says there. And [regarding] cataracts in the eye, Rabbi Akiva says that if they ascended [the altar], they do not descend, because [such a blemish] is fit in a bird [offering]; this proves that it is considered [a case where] its disqualification is in the sacred, even though [cataracts] can exist prior to consecration! And it seems [correct] to explain that wherever something similar to it is fit in another context, it is called "its disqualification is in the sacred": and [an animal] slaughtered at night has [an instance of] fitness in [the burning of] limbs and fats; and [an offering] whose blood went outside [the curtains], for [going outside] is fit in the case of sacrificial portions, and sacrificial portions [that went outside], for [going outside] is fit on a high place (bamah); and [an offering] whose blood was spilled, since its collection [of blood] was performed in fitness, it is called "its disqualification is in the sacred." And the phrasing "its disqualification is in the sacred" means that there is no absolute disqualification here, but rather it was disqualified within its sanctity. And so it is implied [by the fact] that [the Gemara] objects there: What is different regarding left [hand], which has [an instance of] fitness on Yom Kippur, and night, [which has an instance of fitness] with limbs and fats — and therefore they do not defile, as it is "their disqualification in the sacred."

Tosafot on Niddah 41a:5:1.hebrew: היינו דאיצטריך תרי קראי - וא"ת: וליבעי ג' קראי בכל הפסולין, כמו בטרפה דחשיב הכא בהדייהו; דבפרק קמא דמנחות (דף ו.) מצריך ב' קראי בטרפה: חד לנטרפה קודם הקדשה, וחד לנטרפה לאחר הקדשה, ואפילו הכי איצטריך הכא למעוטי מזאת דאם עלתה תרד. וה"נ בשאר פסולין, ליבעי תרי קראי בלא קרא דזאת: חד לקודם הקדש וחד לאחר הקדש דלא יעלו, וקרא דזאת לירדו? ויש לומר: כיון דגלי לן קרא בטרפה, ה"ה לשאר פסולים:
Tosafot on Niddah 41a:5:1.english: That is why two verses were necessary - And if you say: Let three verses be required for all the disqualified [offerings], just as for a *tereifah*, which [the baraita] enumerates here along with them; for in the first chapter of Menachot (6a), [the Gemara] requires two verses regarding a *tereifah*: one for [an animal that] became a *tereifah* prior to its consecration, and one for [an animal that] became a *tereifah* after its consecration; and even so, it was necessary here to exclude [it] from "This" (*zot*), [teaching] that if it ascended [the altar], it must descend. And so too regarding the other disqualified [offerings], let two verses be required aside from the verse of "This": one for [disqualification occurring] prior to consecration and one for after consecration, [teaching] that they may not ascend; and the verse of "This" [to teach] that they must descend? And it may be answered: Since the verse revealed [this] to us regarding a *tereifah*, the same applies to the other disqualified [offerings].

Tosafot on Niddah 41a:6:1.hebrew: קסבר ולדות קדשים בהוייתן הן קדושים - פרש"י דל"ג ליה, דהא כ"ש למ"ד במעי אמן הן קדושים דאיצטריך למעוטי מזאת. ונראה דגרס ליה, ולרבותא נקטיה, דאע"ג דבהויתן הן קדושים ולא קדם הקדשן לפסולן, אצטריך קרא למעוטי, כיון דהפסול לא בא תחלה אלא בבת אחת. אבל לא מצי למגרס קסבר במעי אמן הן קדושים, דהא בסוף פרק דם שחיטה (כריתות דף כג:) קאמר דקסבר ר"ש בהויתן הן קדושים. וכן מוכח משמעתין, דמוקי קרא דזאת לבהמת קדשים, ואתנן ומחיר לא אשכחן אחר הקדש, אפי' לרבי יוסי הגלילי דאמר קדשים קלים ממון הדיוט הוא, דאמר בפרק מי שהיה טמא (פסחים דף צ.) לכל נדר פרט לנדור שאין אתנן חל עלייהו, ולא משכחת אלא בולדות קדשים וכמ"ד בהויתן הן קדושים ונתנם לזונה בעודם בבטן, והכי מוקי לה בפ' פרת חטאת (זבחים דף קיד.), וכן פ"ה. וא"ת, דבשילהי תמורה (דף לג:) תנן: אלו הן הנקברים: קדשים שהפילו, וחולין שנשחטו בעזרה, ור"ש אומר: חולין שנשחטו בעזרה ישרפו; משמע דלא פליג אקדשים שהפילו, וכיון דבהוייתן הן קדושים, אמאי יקברו? והלא אין קדושה חלה עלייהו, כדתנן פרק כיצד מערימין (תמורה דף כד:) רשב"ג אומר: ילדה טומטום ואנדרוגינוס, אין קדושה חלה עלייהו, וקאמר דקסבר דבהויתן הן קדושים, ואפילו קדושת דמים אין חלה עלייהו, דאי חלה, הא אמר בפרק אלו קדשים (תמורה דף יט:) מגו דנחתא קדושת דמים נחתא נמי קדושת הגוף, ואם כן קדשים שהפילו דאסורים בהנאה, לרבי שמעון אמאי? ויש לומר, דפליג גם ארישא, אלא דלא נחת לפלוגי אלא בחולין שנשחטו בעזרה. תדע, דהא חשיב התם נמי בשר בחלב בקבורה, ולרבי שמעון שרי בהנאה בפ"ק דבכורות (דף י.). א"נ י"ל, דנפל קדושה חלה עלויה טפי מטומטום ואנדרוגינוס, משום דאי הוה בר קיימא היה ראוי לקרבן. וא"ת: כיון דסבר בהויתן הן קדושים, היאך קדושה חלה על יוצא דופן וכלאים, דמ"ש מטומטום ואנדרוגינוס? וי"ל, דמיירי כגון שהקדישן בפה קודם שנולדו, דאע"ג דאין קדושת אמן חלה עליהם, קדושת פה חלה עליהם. מיהו מתני' דכיצד מערימין (תמורה דף כד:) משמע דאפילו בקדושת פה אין קדושה חלה עליהם. ועוד, דבשילהי פ"ב דתמורה (דף יז.) קאמר אי אתה מוצא אלא בולדות קדשים ואליבא דרבי יהודה, ואמאי? לא משכחת בהקדישו בפה? ושמא י"ל, דדווקא טומטום ואנדרוגינוס אין קדושה חלה עליהם:
Tosafot on Niddah 41a:6:1.english: He maintains that the offspring of consecrated animals become sacred upon their emergence - Rashi explained that we do not read this [in the text], for all the more so according to the one who maintains [that] they become sacred in their mother's womb was it necessary to exclude [it] from "This" [is the law of the burnt offering] (Leviticus 6:2). And it appears [to us] that one should read it [in the text], and it was stated as a novelty: that even though they become sacred upon their emergence, and their consecration did not precede their disqualification, the verse was necessary to exclude [it], since the disqualification did not come first [either], but rather simultaneously [with the consecration]. However, one cannot read [instead], "He maintains that they become sacred in their mother's womb," because at the end of the chapter [entitled] "Dam Shechita" (Keritot 23b), [the Gemara] says that Rabbi Shimon maintains that they become sacred upon their emergence. And so too is proven from our sugya, which establishes the verse of "This" as referring to a consecrated animal, and an etnan (harlot's hire) and a mechir (price of a dog) we do not find after consecration, even according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who says that lesser-grade offerings (kodashim kalim) are private property — for [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] "Mi Shehayah Tamei" (Pesachim 90a): "[For any vow] to any vow" (Deuteronomy 23:19) excludes that which is already vowed, [teaching] that an etnan does not take effect upon them; and you find [such a case] only with the offspring of consecrated animals, and according to the one who maintains that they become sacred upon their emergence, where he gave them to a prostitute while they were still in the womb. And this is how [the Gemara] establishes it in the chapter [entitled] "Parat Chatat" (Zevachim 114a); and so Rashi explained. And if you say: For at the end of Temurah (33b) we learned: "These are those that are buried: Consecrated animals that miscarried, and non-sacred animals that were slaughtered in the Temple courtyard. And Rabbi Shimon says: Non-sacred animals that were slaughtered in the Temple courtyard shall be burned." This implies that he does not disagree regarding consecrated animals that miscarried; and since they become sacred upon their emergence, why should they be buried? Is it not so that no sanctity takes effect upon them? As we learned in the chapter [entitled] "Keitzad Maarimin" (Temurah 24b): "Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: If it gave birth to a tumtum (an animal of indeterminate sex) or an androgynos (a hermaphrodite), no sanctity takes effect upon them." And [the Gemara there] says that he maintains that they become sacred upon their emergence, and even sanctity of value (kedushat damim) does not take effect upon them — for if it did take effect, didn't [the Gemara] say in the chapter [entitled] "Elu Kodashim" (Temurah 19b): "Since sanctity of value descended, bodily sanctity (kedushat ha-guf) also descended"? And if so, regarding consecrated animals that miscarried, which are forbidden for benefit — according to Rabbi Shimon, why [should they be forbidden]? And one can say that he disagrees with the first clause as well, but he set out to dispute only regarding non-sacred animals slaughtered in the Temple courtyard. Know [that this is so], for it also counts meat [cooked] in milk there among [the items requiring] burial, and according to Rabbi Shimon, [meat in milk] is permitted for benefit in the first chapter of Bekhorot (10a). Alternatively, one can say that upon a miscarriage (nefel), sanctity takes effect more than upon a tumtum and an androgynos, because had it been viable (bar kayama), it would have been fit for a sacrifice. And if you say: Since he maintains that they become sacred upon their emergence, how does sanctity take effect upon a caesarean-born animal (yotzei dofen) and [an offspring of] diverse kinds (kilayim)? For what is the difference between [them and] a tumtum and an androgynos? And one can say that it deals with [a case] where, for example, he consecrated them orally (be-feh) before they were born; for even though the sanctity of their mother does not take effect upon them, sanctity [bestowed] orally does take effect upon them. However, the mishna in [the chapter entitled] "Keitzad Maarimin" (Temurah 24b) implies that even with oral consecration, sanctity does not take effect upon them. And furthermore, at the end of the second chapter of Temurah (17a), [the Gemara] says: "You find [this] only with the offspring of consecrated animals, and according to Rabbi Yehuda" — and why? Could you not find [it] where he consecrated it orally? And perhaps one can say that specifically upon a tumtum and an androgynos does sanctity not take effect:
